title: Stop a slow command in a bash script after a set number of seconds
summary: Runs any command with a time limit. If the command takes longer, it is stopped and the script reports a timeout, so a hung program cannot block the whole script forever.

warnings: A stopped command gets no chance to clean up. A program that writes a file halfway can leave a damaged file behind.
Choose a limit longer than the normal run time. Otherwise a slow but correct run is stopped too.
timeout is part of GNU coreutils. On macOS, install coreutils with Homebrew and use the name gtimeout instead.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-with-timeout.sh - run a command, but stop it after SECONDS.
# Usage: ./run-with-timeout.sh SECONDS COMMAND [ARGS...]
# Exit code: the command's own exit code, 124 when it timed out, 2 for bad usage.

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# < 2 )) || ! [[ $1 =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 SECONDS COMMAND [ARGS...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
LIMIT=$1
shift

# timeout sends TERM after LIMIT seconds. -k 5 sends KILL 5 seconds later
# if the command ignores TERM.
status=0
timeout -k 5 "$LIMIT" "$@" || status=$?

if (( status == 124 )); then
    echo "timed out after ${LIMIT}s: $*" >&2
elif (( status != 0 )); then
    echo "command failed with exit code $status: $*" >&2
fi
exit "$status"

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
